complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement Core Domain Models and Publisher Interface
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Task 1 into subtasks covering: 1) MessageState sealed class with transition validation logic, 2) OutboxMessage data class with kotlinx-serialization annotations and default values, 3) InboxMessage data class with idempotency key fields, 4) Destination sealed interface with Http and RabbitMQ variants, 5) Publisher and InboxReceiver interfaces with Result types. Include updating core/build.gradle.kts to add kotlinx-serialization and kotlinx-datetime dependencies from the version catalog.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This is greenfield development with well-defined data classes. The core module currently has only a placeholder main function, so everything needs to be created from scratch. However, the task involves straightforward Kotlin data classes and sealed classes/interfaces with no external dependencies beyond kotlinx-serialization (already in version catalog). The complexity comes from ensuring proper serialization annotations and designing the state transition logic correctly. Unit testing is straightforward with standard assertions.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Extend Configuration System with Full PRD Schema
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Task 2 into subtasks covering: 1) Extend QueueBoxConfig.kt with DatabaseConfig, OutboxConfig (polling/retry), InboxConfig data classes, 2) Add DestinationConfig sealed class with Http and RabbitMQ variants using @SerialName annotations, 3) Add RouteConfig and SourceConfig data classes for topic-based routing, 4) Create ConfigValidator.kt with validation rules for database URLs, port ranges, and destination references, 5) Update queuebox.yml with full example configuration and test env var substitution with Hoplite's ${VAR} syntax.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: The config module already has a working ConfigLoader using Hoplite and a basic QueueBoxConfig. This task extends the existing code rather than starting from scratch. The complexity involves correctly designing the sealed class hierarchy with kotlinx-serialization polymorphic annotations (@SerialName), ensuring Hoplite's env var substitution works, and implementing validation logic. The existing Hoplite ecosystem bundle in build.gradle.kts should handle most configuration needs.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement PostgreSQL Repository Layer with Connection Pooling
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Task 3 into subtasks covering: 1) Update postgres/build.gradle.kts with HikariCP, PostgreSQL driver, Exposed ORM, and TestContainers dependencies, 2) Create DatabaseFactory.kt with HikariDataSource configuration and Exposed Database.connect, 3) Create Tables.kt with OutboxTable and InboxTable Exposed table definitions including JSONB support and unique constraints, 4) Implement OutboxRepository with claimBatch using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, markSent, markFailed, scheduleRetry, markDead methods, 5) Implement InboxRepository with store (using insertIgnore for deduplication) and claimPending methods, 6) Create SQL migration scripts V1__create_outbox.sql and V2__create_inbox.sql, 7) Write integration tests using TestContainers PostgreSQL for concurrent claiming and deduplication scenarios.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This is high complexity because: 1) The postgres module is currently empty (just placeholder), requiring full greenfield development, 2) Multiple new dependencies need to be added (HikariCP, Exposed ORM, PostgreSQL driver, TestContainers), 3) Implementing FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED requires understanding PostgreSQL-specific features and Exposed's ForUpdateOption, 4) Concurrent testing with coroutines is non-trivial, 5) JSONB handling with Exposed requires exposed-json module configuration. The integration testing with TestContainers adds operational complexity.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement Outbox Poller with Topic-Based Routing and Retry Strategy
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Task 4 into subtasks covering: 1) Update outbox-service/build.gradle.kts with dependencies on core, config, postgres modules and kotlinx-coroutines, 2) Implement RetryStrategy.kt with exponential backoff calculation including jitter and max delay capping, 3) Implement MessageRouter.kt with glob pattern matching (*, **) for topic-based routing and routing key template rendering, 4) Implement OutboxPoller.kt with coroutine-based polling loop using SupervisorJob, batch claiming, and coordinated publisher dispatch, 5) Add graceful shutdown handling with coroutine cancellation and in-flight message completion, 6) Write unit tests for RetryStrategy and MessageRouter, plus integration test with mock repository.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This is moderately high complexity. The outbox-service module is empty. Key challenges: 1) Implementing glob pattern matching with proper regex conversion (tricky edge cases), 2) Coroutine lifecycle management with SupervisorJob and proper cancellation, 3) Coordinating multiple publishers and handling partial failures, 4) The polling loop needs careful error handling to avoid infinite retry loops. Depends on Tasks 1, 2, 3 being complete which adds integration risk.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement HTTP Publisher for Outbox Delivery
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Task 5 into subtasks covering: 1) Update outbox-service/build.gradle.kts with Ktor client dependencies (ktor-client-core, ktor-client-cio, ktor-client-content-negotiation), 2) Implement HttpPublisher.kt with client pooling per destination, proper header injection (X-Message-Id, X-Topic, X-Attempt), and Result-based error handling, 3) Create HttpPublishException with statusCode and body fields for detailed error reporting, 4) Write integration tests using Ktor testApplication or WireMock for success, timeout, and error response scenarios.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity. Ktor client is already in the version catalog (though need client-specific modules added). The implementation is straightforward HTTP client usage with proper error handling. Key challenges: 1) Managing multiple HttpClient instances with connection pooling, 2) Proper timeout configuration (connect vs request), 3) Testing requires mock HTTP server setup. The codebase already uses Ktor server, so patterns will be familiar.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement HTTP Inbox Receiver with Idempotency Extraction
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Task 6 into subtasks covering: 1) Update inbox-service/build.gradle.kts with dependencies on core, config, postgres, Ktor server ecosystem, and json-path library, 2) Implement IdempotencyExtractor.kt using JSONPath for extracting idempotency keys from arbitrary JSON payloads, 3) Implement InboxHandler.kt coordinating extraction, message building, and repository storage with proper result handling, 4) Implement InboxRoutes.kt Ktor route installer that dynamically registers routes based on configured sources, 5) Write unit tests for IdempotencyExtractor and integration tests with Ktor testApplication for webhook receipt, duplicate detection, and error scenarios.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate-high complexity. The inbox-service module is empty. Challenges: 1) JSONPath library integration (json-path:2.9.0) requires careful handling of missing paths and type coercion, 2) Dynamic route registration based on config requires understanding Ktor's routing DSL, 3) The sealed class result hierarchy (InboxHandlerResult) needs proper HTTP status code mapping. The integration testing with Ktor testApplication is well-documented but requires setup.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement Application Wiring with Health Checks and Metrics
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Task 7 into subtasks covering: 1) Refactor App.kt main function to wire all components with proper dependency injection (repositories, publishers, handlers), 2) Implement HealthManager.kt with database connectivity check and extensible component health reporting, 3) Implement HealthRoutes.kt with /health endpoint returning appropriate HTTP status codes, 4) Implement MetricsCollector.kt with atomic counters for messages processed/failed/received and Prometheus-format export, 5) Implement MetricsRoutes.kt with /metrics endpoint, 6) Add graceful shutdown handling with Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook ensuring in-flight message completion.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate-high complexity primarily due to coordination. The app module has a basic Ktor skeleton but needs significant expansion. Challenges: 1) Manual dependency injection wiring can be error-prone with many components, 2) Shutdown hook needs careful sequencing (stop poller → wait for in-flight → close connections), 3) Prometheus metrics format requires specific formatting. This task is mostly integration work but requires understanding all previous components.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Create Docker Configuration and Compose Setup
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Task 8 into subtasks covering: 1) Create multi-stage Dockerfile with gradle:8.11-jdk23 builder stage and eclipse-temurin:23-jre-alpine runtime stage with non-root user, 2) Create docker-compose.yml with queuebox, postgres, and optional rabbitmq services including health checks and volume mounts, 3) Create docker-compose.override.yml for local development with live-reload support, 4) Create .dockerignore and update queuebox.yml with environment variable placeholders for containerized deployment.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity. No Docker infrastructure exists yet, but the task is well-defined standard Docker/Compose patterns. The multi-stage build for Kotlin/Gradle is straightforward. Key considerations: 1) Ensuring the Gradle installDist output structure matches the ENTRYPOINT, 2) Health check timing and dependencies between services, 3) Volume mounting for SQL migrations. The project uses JDK 23 which requires attention to base image availability.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement RabbitMQ Publisher with Connection Management
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Task 9 into subtasks covering: 1) Update rabbitmq/build.gradle.kts with amqp-client, kotlinx-coroutines, and TestContainers RabbitMQ dependencies, 2) Implement RabbitConnection.kt with ConnectionFactory configuration, automatic recovery settings, and Mutex-protected channel creation, 3) Implement RabbitPublisher.kt with connection pooling, exchange declaration, publisher confirms, and routing key template rendering, 4) Create RabbitPublishException for detailed error reporting, 5) Write integration tests using TestContainers RabbitMQ for connection management, message publishing with confirms, and auto-reconnection scenarios.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity. The rabbitmq module is empty. Challenges: 1) RabbitMQ Java client has blocking APIs that need coroutine wrapping with Dispatchers.IO, 2) Publisher confirms require waitForConfirms which can block, 3) Connection/channel lifecycle management with auto-recovery is complex, 4) Testing auto-reconnection requires container restart which is flaky in CI. The amqp-client library is mature but requires careful thread-safety handling.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement RabbitMQ Consumer for Inbox Ingestion
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Task 10 into subtasks covering: 1) Implement RabbitConsumer.kt with DefaultConsumer, prefetch configuration, and coroutine-based message processing, 2) Implement idempotency key extraction from headers (x-idempotency-key) with fallback to payload JSONPath and messageId, 3) Implement proper ack/nack handling with requeue on storage failures, 4) Extend SourceConfig in config module to support RabbitMQ source type with sealed class polymorphism, 5) Write integration tests for message consumption, deduplication, ack/nack behavior, and prefetch limiting.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity. Builds on Task 9's RabbitConnection. Challenges: 1) DefaultConsumer callback runs on RabbitMQ's dispatcher thread, requiring careful coroutine bridging, 2) Ack/nack semantics with requeue have subtle edge cases (infinite requeue loops), 3) The config schema extension requires careful polymorphic serialization setup, 4) Testing prefetch behavior requires observing message flow timing. Dependencies on Tasks 3, 6, and 9 increase integration risk.
